steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift to feel like objects.
Strong depth shows a menu or dialog sits above vivid sections. Without a shadow it blends into the color blocks.

steps.rule: The see-through layer behind a modal.
pick: black.light.scrim: a see-through layer that dims the page behind a modal, so the dialog is the one thing to act on.
darkPick: black.dark.scrim: a see-through layer that dims the page behind a modal, so the dialog is the one thing to act on.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs and raised cards in dark, in order to show height by tone,

on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So visitors see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 24px offset and a 48px blur at 20%, larger than the card's. So a menu sits clearly above vivid sections and cards, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are pronounced (elevation.values).
darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 24px offset and 48px blur, at 60% black instead of 20%. So a menu still sits above dark sections, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

pick: radius.24: We use a 24px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each offer read as a separate object, in a bold tone by brand convention. A large radius does this by breaking the outline with a wide curve while the sides stay straight. So each offer reads as one friendly object, because containers get their own corner (shape.count) and the brand is bold (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line,

on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So visitors see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line,

on surface.raised (#4D3A33, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So visitors see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Larger icons hold their own next to big type.

steps.use: Button secondary, then confirm with Button danger

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
pick: on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone,

under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

pick: radius.12: We use the 12px box corner for boxes that grow in order to keep them box-shaped objects by the relation: a pill control gives way to the box corner. A moderate radius does this by curving the corners while the sides stay straight as the box grows. So a text area or a list item stays a box, not an oval, because controls are pills (shape.values) and the brand is bold (brand.q1).
